title: What happens at the cutoff?
hook: Separate a treatment jump from the smooth trend through the threshold.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: students just above and below a test-score cutoff are alike; the jump at the line is the effect.

misconception: Treating scholarship cutoff as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: students just above and below a test-score cutoff are alike; the jump at the line is the effect.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: A toy score rule gives outcome score/10, plus 3 for scores at least 50. What discontinuity at the threshold belongs to treatment, after accounting for the smooth baseline?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-scholarship-cutoff/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Scores [48,49,50,51,52], baseline outcome score/10. Treatment at score>=50 adds3. Show untreated smooth line and treatment jump3; moving cutoff changes eligibility, not specified effect.

claims.text: The scholarship rule retains a threshold jump of 3; the no-treatment comparison retains 0. The adjacent observed scores differ by 3.1 because the smooth baseline also changes by 0.1.

claims.text: A regression-discontinuity interpretation separates the jump from that smooth trend. It requires continuity of untreated outcomes and no precise sorting or other change at the same cutoff.
